subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: Should a QQ Bot C2C approval callback require an explicit non-wildcard authorized actor, or may the exact recipient of that approval prompt approve without an allowlist entry?
rationale: Current documentation and merged hardening require explicit authorization, while the linked PR treats all direct conversations as trusted even though dmPolicy can admit wildcard senders; repository evidence cannot safely choose that authorization boundary without maintainer intent and QQ identity guarantees.

options.title: Bind To Prompt Recipient
options.body: Permit implicit C2C approval only when the callback actor is securely matched to the exact recipient recorded for that approval request, while retaining explicit authorization elsewhere.

options.title: Keep Explicit Authorization
options.body: Retain the current non-wildcard allowlist requirement and improve setup guidance and immediate unauthorized feedback so requests do not appear to malfunction.

options.title: Trust All Direct Chats
options.body: Accept the linked PR's unconditional C2C bypass, intentionally granting approval authority to any direct-chat actor admitted by the active DM policy.

recommendation.title: Bind To Prompt Recipient
recommendation.body: Permit implicit C2C approval only when the callback actor is securely matched to the exact recipient recorded for that approval request, while retaining explicit authorization elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged approval-auth hardening most directly defines the security invariant under reconsideration.
